items.a: Start with consulting when the problem is unclear, the system already exists, or multiple build paths are possible. Start with development when the scope, architecture, and success criteria are already defined.
items.q: When should we start with consulting instead of development?

items.a: A technical audit can cover architecture, performance, SEO implementation, Core Web Vitals, security surface, deployment flow, dependencies, CMS setup, integrations, and code maintainability.
items.q: What can a technical audit include?

items.a: Yes. The audit is designed to produce a roadmap that can be implemented by Altruvex, your internal team, or another developer — you keep the findings and recommendations either way. If you do go on to build with us, we credit {auditCredit} against the project price; if you don't, the fee stands and the roadmap is still yours.
items.q: Can we use the audit without hiring Altruvex for the build?

items.a: Most focused audits take five business days after access and context are provided. Larger systems may need a longer discovery window if there are multiple codebases, integrations, or stakeholders.

hero.title: Design you
hero.description: We translate your offer into sharper hierarchy, clearer messaging and one direct path — and every decision behind it is a rule you can check, not a taste you have to trust.
hero.card: Six disciplines, one system — every screen built by rule, not by taste.

items.title: One screen, one job.
items.body: Every page is built around the one action it exists for. Everything else on it either supports that action or leaves.

items.title: The flow comes before the frame.
items.body: We map how a buyer moves through the site — where they arrive, what they need, where they decide — before a single screen is drawn.

items.title: Hierarchy you can measure.
items.body: Size, weight and contrast follow one scale, so the most important thing on a screen wins first — by rule, not by taste.

items.title: Your identity, as a system.
items.body: Colour, type and spacing become rules your team can extend — not a style that drifts the first time someone edits a page.

items.title: Fast is a design decision.
items.body: Every image, font and animation is weighed against load time before it ships. A beautiful screen that loads late is a screen nobody sees.

items.title: Readable by everyone.
items.body: WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and structure, checked in Arabic and in English — a requirement of the design, not a fix after launch.
